title: Math Functions

lines.explanation:
The Math class in the java.lang package provides methods and 
constants for doing more advanced mathematical computation. 
The methods in the Math class are all static, so you call them 
directly from the class. To use these objects from another class, 
you prefix the class name. abs() method returns the absolute 
value of its input argument. Here, i = 9.

ceil() method returns the smallest integer that is greater than or 
equal to its input argument. The ceiling of every integer is equal to 
the integer itself. Here, j = 5.0.

The sqrt() method returns the correctly rounded positive square root 
of a double value. Here, squareroot = 30.0.

The pow() method contains two input parameters. They are 
respectively the base and the exponent values. pow = 9.0.

The round() method returns the closest integer to the input 
argument. Here, the value of round is equal to 20 .
